subject: Re: Latency vs cost — follow-up + pricing ranges

Subject: Latency vs cost — follow-up + next steps

Hi Sal — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and a couple of asks so we can put together a tailored proposal: 

Summary of what you said on the call
- Primary workload: transactional ML assistant (API calls from web + mobile).
- Estimated steady-state token volume: ~150–250M tokens/month. Peak bursts up to ~10–15M tokens/day.
- Latency target: aiming for p95 <= 200ms for user-facing flows; p50 ideally < 100ms.
- Primary constraint: keep unit economics around $15–$25 per 1M tokens to fit internal budget targets.

Key tradeoffs we discussed (latency vs cost)
- Hosted (standard): best time-to-value; streaming enabled; cost-effective for lower SLOs. Typical pricing band we use for this profile: $20–$35 / 1M tokens (depends on model variant and streaming).
- Dedicated pool: reserved GPUs for predictable latency and throughput; lowers unit cost at scale and reduces p95 tail. Estimated band: $12–$20 / 1M tokens once committed capacity is sized for 150–250M tokens/mo.
- Private / on-prem: for strict compliance — higher ops overhead and higher baseline cost.

Performance knobs and impact on unit cost
- Streaming (token-by-token): reduces perceived latency for users; modest increase in compute overhead vs fully batched generation. Good for p50 improvements.
- Batching: increases tokens/sec efficiency (lower $/1M) but increases per-request tail latency; you can tune max batch size and max latency window to balance.
- Continuous / adaptive batching + prefix/KV caching: reduces cost dramatically for repeated prompts (up to 30–50% savings) with minimal latency impact for warm caches.
- SLO-driven routing: route critical requests to low-latency (higher-cost) pools and non-critical to low-cost pools. Allows you to meet strict p95 targets without paying for every request at the premium tier.

Proposal / next steps I need from you
1) Confirm expected monthly tokens (estimate range is fine).
2) Confirm target p95 (is 200ms firm, or would you prefer 150ms?).
3) Budget range you want to present to procurement ($/month or $/1M tokens).
4) If procurement is involved, share contact so we can include them in the commercial/contract thread.

Attaching a quick draft: redwood-proposal-draft.pdf and an XLS with scenario math (pricing-scenarios.xlsx) — this contains 3 pricing scenarios (hosted, dedicated 6-month commit, dedicated 12-month commit) and sample unit economics at 150M / 200M / 250M tokens.

Suggested near-term plan
- Confirm numbers -> we will send a pricing scaffold and recommended config (streaming vs batch, batch windows, routing policy).
- Optional: 2-week dedicated POC with a small reserved pool to validate p95/p50 and cost curves.

If you’re free Wed afternoon I can loop Marcus and Evelyn for a short product/infra Q&A.

Thanks,

Hi Sal / procurement team — answering the bullets and attaching the scenario workbook with explicit math. See the short synopsis below; full numbers are in pricing-scenarios.xlsx.

Confirmed assumptions
- Volumes: we ran scenarios for 100 / 150 / 200M tokens / month as requested.
- Target budget band: $3k–$6k / month -> maps roughly to $15–$30 per 1M tokens depending on model family and whether you enable streaming. See table in the XLS.
- Latency: p95 < 150ms is reachable with a dedicated pool + streaming + conservative batch-window (max window 10ms) for the majority of requests. For the strictest tail (global p99 during big bursts) we recommend SLO-driven routing to reserve a small portion of capacity in a low-latency pool (adds ~10–20% to overall spend but keeps most traffic in cheaper pools).

Three recommended scenarios (high-level)
1) Hosted (no commit) — minimal ops; streaming enabled; conservative batching. Estimated unit cost: $22–$35 / 1M tokens. Expected p50 ~ 80–120ms; p95 ~ 180–300ms (depends on burst).
2) Dedicated 6-month commit (recommended starting point) — reserved capacity sized for 150M tokens/mo. Estimated unit cost: $13–$20 / 1M tokens (depending on exact commit). Expected p50 ~ 50–90ms; p95 ~ 120–180ms with streaming + small batch windows.
3) Dedicated 12-month commit + SLO routing — best unit economics if you want consistent p95 <150ms at scale. Estimated unit cost: $10–$16 / 1M tokens. Includes a small hot pool (10–15% of traffic) for critical flows.

Config knobs we would apply for your workload
- Streaming on by default for UI flows (improves perceived latency).
- Max batch window = 10ms (keeps tail latency low).
- Adaptive batching for background/async flows (max window 100–250ms) to maximize throughput and lower cost.
- Prefix/KV caching for repeated prompts (we’ll instrument to measure hit-rate; could reduce tokens served by 20–40%).
- SLO routing: define critical endpoints (e.g., /assistant/inline) to route to hot pool.

Attachments: pricing-scenarios.xlsx (contains modeled $/1M numbers, monthly totals, and assumptions), redwood-proposal-draft.pdf (commercial draft).

Next steps
- Please confirm which commit horizon you want us to model (monthly, 6-month, 12-month).
- If procurement wants, we can open a side thread for T&Cs and PO requirements.
- Suggest a 30-min technical kickoff on Mon Jun 7 to scope the POC (Marcus / Evelyn can lead infra topics).

I’ll be available Mon morning PT; Marcus and Evelyn are on the thread if you want to pick times.
